newsitem.title: UK: NWE fuel-low sulphur storms ahead, not high sulphu.
newsitem.headline: NWE fuel-low sulphur storms ahead, not high sulphu.

text.p: For the second day running low sulphur cracked fuel broke winter 1991 highs with the market pegged at $129-130 fob NWE, up $9 against this time last week and with further upward potential seen.

A 10 kt cargo of high quality low sulphur sold at $128.50 fob NWE and the remaining large parcel of 40-50 kt tonnes was looking for above $129 fob. Low sulphur cargoes found few interested buyers and prices were put around $125-126 fob ARA.
Tankers of 50 kt were scarce and shipping brokers say rates have risen up to nearly $11 a tonne for trips from NWE into the Mediterranean.
A 1.5 percent sulphur cargo was sold at $116 fob Dunkirk and the buyer was heard to be interested in a 0.37 sulphur cargo.
"I think they want to blend them to make a one percent cargo," said one trader.

While low sulphur surged ahead high sulphur drifted showing only the narrowest of gains, essentially driven by crude rather than fundamentals. High sulphur barges traded at $115 and $116 before edging $1 lower while cargoes were assessed at about $108 fob NWE.
"There is demand, but it's not very vocal," said a dealer.
